title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative: Bangladesh’s labour law and governance frameworks face gaps in alignment with international labour standards (ILS), particularly regarding freedom of association, collective bargaining, labour inspection, and child labour. While the Bangladesh Labour Act (BLA) has undergone reforms, challenges persist in enforcement, application, and gender-responsive, inclusive protection. Labour law lags behind ILS requirements, and child labour remains prevalent, affecting 1.8 million children as of 2022. Bangladesh has ratified 35 ILO Conventions but still needs to ratify instruments such as Conventions 155, 187, 188, 189, and 190. The ILO’s strategy focuses on supporting the Government in aligning labour laws and rules with ILS, ensuring they are effectively applied, inclusive, and gender-responsive. ILO assists in conducting gap analyses, developing ratification plans for pending Conventions, and supporting the implementation of the GB Roadmap and the National Action Plan on Labour Sector Reform. This includes targeted technical support for BLA amendments, stakeholder consultations, and capacity building for tripartite mechanisms to engage in ILS reporting and application. ILO supports the implementation of the National Plan of Action (2020–2025) on child labour, focusing on knowledge and capacity building, expanding the Child Labour Monitoring System, and promoting safe work initiatives for youth. Expected results include increased national capacity to ratify and apply ILS, strengthened tripartite engagement in normative processes, and expanded protection of fundamental principles and rights at work. Women workers, child labourers, youth, workers in formal and informal sectors, and employers are primary beneficiaries. Key partners include the Ministry of Labour and Employment, Department of Labour, Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments, Bangladesh Employers’ Federation, trade unions, chambers of commerce, UN agencies, and development partners.
